meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Моя камбала там не постарела, а?

meanings.en: to get divorced, dissolve a marriage
meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'вестись'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'got divorced', paired with 'разводиться'.

examples.trans: Let's get a divorce.

examples.text: Они решили развестись после десяти лет брака.
examples.trans: They decided to divorce after ten years of marriage.
I will divorce you!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'until', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Don't touch my dish!
You have really gotten on everyone's nerves already.

examples.text: Мне стыдно ваше блюдо в зал нести.
examples.trans: I am ashamed to carry your dish into the dining room.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'видание'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'goodbye' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Kristina Semyonovna, goodbye!
Goodbye!
I have a date today.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'fourteenth', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Page fourteen!

examples.text: Макс сказал это совершенно четырнадцатый и спокойно.
examples.trans: Max said this quite fourteenth and calmly.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'траница'). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common feminine noun meaning 'page' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Page fourteen!
And on the second page as well.

examples.trans: Come on, cook faster!

meanings.en: to run (in one direction), to flee, to escape

examples.text: Надо бежать! Беги в деревню к маме.
